summary: This RFC suggests a simple way for a workstation to fetch mail from a mailbox server, with sending done through SMTP. It is the first version of the Post Office Protocol and was replaced by RFC 937.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 918 describes how a computer asks a mail server for all the messages in a mailbox. The user can choose to leave the messages on the server or request their deletion after they arrive.

subtitle: A TCP protocol for a workstation to retrieve mail from a mailbox server.

tldr.problem: A user's workstation needs a way to access mail held on a mailbox server.
tldr.mechanism: The client connects over TCP, identifies itself with USER and PASS, and retrieves all mail in a mailbox with RETR or RDEL. RDEL marks the mail for deletion after receipt is confirmed.
tldr.outcome: RFC 918 describes the first Post Office Protocol and was replaced by RFC 937.

today: RFC 918 was replaced by RFC 937, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Purpose and Connection
sections.content: The Post Office Protocol lets a user's workstation access mail held by a mailbox server. The RFC expects mail to be sent from the workstation to the server using the Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP). This protocol depends on TCP.
sections.plainLanguage: A computer connects to a mail server to collect messages. SMTP is expected to handle sending mail in the other direction.

sections.title: Logging In and Choosing a Mailbox
sections.content: The server listens for a connection and sends a greeting when a client connects. The client sends USER with a name, followed by PASS with a password. It then starts a transaction for a named mailbox using RETR to read the mail without deleting it, or RDEL to read and delete it.
sections.plainLanguage: The client gives its user name and password, then chooses a mailbox. RETR leaves its messages in place; RDEL requests deletion after delivery.

sections.title: Receiving Mail and Ending the Session
sections.content: The server opens and locks the mailbox and reports the number of characters it contains. The client sends RCEV when ready for the data, then sends RCVD after receiving and accepting it. For an RDEL transaction, the server then deletes the mail if the operation succeeds; it closes and unlocks the mailbox in either case. QUIT ends the session.
sections.plainLanguage: The server sends the mail after the client asks for it. The client confirms receipt, and the server closes the mailbox and connection when the session ends.
